text:
Alex Chen: Quick sync — need a decision on how we model reserved capacity transfers + limits for long commitments. Customer A wants a 12‑mo commit but the org wants to reassign credits between teams mid-contract. Do we allow transfer, or keep a strict reservation window?
Maria Gonzales: Can we do soft transfers? like a two-step: request transfer -> approve by account owner -> settle pro rata charges. keeps us from manual ops. :thinking_face: 
Samir Patel: Pro rata makes sense but watch edge cases: overlapping transfers and burst credits. If we allow transfers, we need a clear entitlement ledger to avoid double-spend.
Keiko Tanaka: +1 on ledger. Also need feature gating: some add-ons (priority lane, retained KV cache) shouldn't be freely transferrable unless higher-tier SLA is maintained.
Alex Chen: Good point. Customer asks also include per-route hard limits vs pooled entitlements. They want to cap a single team to 20% of commit.
Maria Gonzales: Proposal A: reservation window model — commit creates a time-bound pool assigned to the org; transfers allowed with approvals, transfers consume a small transfer fee, and limits can be applied per-team via policy.
Samir Patel: Proposal B: entitlement buckets — each team gets named buckets at signup; admin can reassign whole buckets, but we block fractional transfers. simpler accounting but less flexible for customers who want dynamic rebalancing.
Keiko Tanaka: UX + billing tradeoffs: buckets => invoice line items per bucket. Reservations => single invoice with internal transfer records. Buckets are easier for auditing.
Alex Chen: We need to capture launch criteria: 1) automated transfer flow in Console 2) audit trail in billing 3) per-route limit enforcement and test harness 4) legal-approved T&Cs for transfer policy.
Maria Gonzales: Risks: transfer abuse (resale), accounting edge cases for refunds, and quota starvation if transfers are slow. Mitigations: transfer caps (max X% per 30d), transfer cooldowns, admin approval.
Samir Patel: Implementation note: backend needs an entitlement ledger table with columns: `bucket_id`, `org_id`, `team_id`, `committed_units`, `available_units`, `locked_for_transfer` — we can prototype migration in 2 sprints. Sample migration SQL snippet:```sql
BEGIN;
ALTER TABLE commitments ADD COLUMN bucket_id uuid;
UPDATE commitments SET bucket_id = gen_random_uuid() WHERE bucket_id IS NULL;
COMMIT;
```
Keiko Tanaka: For ops: we should add a fallback autopolicy to split traffic to lower-tier model if per-route hard limit exceeded instead of outright 403. Keeps customer apps alive.
ProductBot: Linked doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/pricing/entitlement-shaping-draft (editable)
Alex Chen: Decision call? leaning to hybrid: default to buckets for auditability + optional ephemeral reservation window for short-term rebalancing (<=7 days) with fee and admin approval. This satisfies accounting and gives flexibility.
Maria Gonzales: Sounds good. Action items: Maria to draft console flows + UI copy, Samir to size backend ledger + migration (2 sprints), Keiko to define autopolicy fallback rules, Legal to review transfer T&Cs (I'll ping them).
Samir Patel: I'll put a quick spike on my board and add the SQL PR placeholder.
Keiko Tanaka: I'll draft fallback behavior doc and example rate-limits.
Alex Chen: OK let's run this in the next roadmap sync. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
